page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server within the n1 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. This configuration consists of 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, supported by 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding 0.9 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes an L3 cache of 45 MB, alongside L1d and L2 caches of 32 KB and 0.25 MB respectively. It supports hardware features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES cryptography, and Bit Manipulation Instruction Set 2 (BMI2). No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the n1-highcpu-2 demonstrates entry-level performance characteristics. Its stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1086.39, while the multi-core score reaches 1408.88. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.82 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 13.22 GB/sec for large-block reads and 11.3 GB/sec for large-block writes. The instance achieved a Passmark CPU score of 1638.85 and a memory score of 730.43. For application-specific tasks, it handles 1.35 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers 1.51 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Small-scale LLM inference using a 135M model yields 65.68 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 38.74 tokens/sec for text generation.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-2 is its highly constrained memory capacity of 2.0 GB relative to its 2 dedicated vCPUs, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications. From a cost-efficiency perspective, it offers a low-cost entry point for compute-bound workloads that do not require large datasets in memory. This instance is best suited for lightweight background workers, basic web serving, simple scripting, and software development or testing environments that require dedicated CPU resources without high memory overhead.
